subject: Culture
title: The First Job
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The First Job.

hook.text: Your first paycheck changes something. Money you earned yourself feels different from money you were given.

buildup.text: In most industrial societies, the first job is the real coming-of-age moment. It signals independence.

discovery.text: Anthropologist David Graeber noted that modern work fills the ritual gap that traditional rites left behind.

twist.text: In Japan, new hires attend company entrance ceremonies—suits, speeches, and bowing. The job is the initiation.

climax.text: Without formal coming-of-age rituals, modern cultures use work to mark the shift from youth to adult.

punchline.text: The first paycheck is the modern rite of passage.

quiz.question: What did anthropologist David Graeber argue about modern work?
options: It fills the gap left by traditional rites of passage
